QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_19

question.text: On the National Stock Exchange (NSE), the contract cycle for equity index and stock futures consists of:

answer.text: Three monthly contracts - the near month, next month, and far month - with new contracts introduced on the trading day following expiry of the near month contract
Four quarterly contracts expiring in March, June, September, and December of each year
Weekly contracts that expire every Friday, with four contracts available at any given time
Two monthly contracts - the current month and next month only

explanation.text: The Logic: NSE index and stock futures follow a three-month trading cycle. At any point there are three contracts available — the near month, the next month, and the far month. On the trading day following the expiry of the near-month contract, a new far-month contract is introduced so that three months are always quoted. The Trap: Quarterly-only cycles are used in some other markets, not for NSE equity futures. The cycle is three months, not two. Note: Equity-derivative product menus differ across exchanges — for example, the workbook notes that BSE offers monthly as well as weekly futures contracts — so avoid blanket claims that weekly contracts are never offered on equity futures.
